title: God's Promises — Searchable Canon Seed
translationNote: Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (public domain). Paraphrase fields are original plain-language summaries for searchability, not additional Bible text.
expandHint: Add books systematically: continue Exodus–Deuteronomy, Historicals, Wisdom, Prophets, Gospels, Epistles, Revelation. Feelings tags support emotion-first search; keep pastoral accuracy.

promises.promise: God blesses humanity with fruitfulness and entrusts them with dominion over the earth and its creatures.
promises.text: God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
promises.context: Spoken at creation after God made humankind in his image.

promises.promise: God provides food from the earth’s plants and fruit-bearing trees.
promises.text: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.”
promises.context: God’s provision for humanity in the garden world he made.

promises.promise: God promises that the woman’s offspring will crush the serpent’s head, even as the serpent strikes his heel—the first gospel promise of victory over evil.
promises.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.
promises.context: God’s judgment on the serpent after the fall in Eden.

promises.promise: God commits never again to curse the ground as he did, nor to strike down every living thing as in the flood.
promises.text: The LORD smelled the pleasant aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake because the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth. I will never again strike every living thing, as I have done.”
promises.context: After Noah’s burnt offering when the flood waters had receded.

promises.promise: As long as the earth remains, God will keep the rhythms of seasons, day and night unbroken.
promises.text: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.
promises.context: God’s inner resolve after the flood, assuring stable order for life on earth.

promises.promise: After the flood, God again blesses humanity to be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
promises.text: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.”
promises.context: God’s first words to Noah’s family after they leave the ark.

promises.promise: God establishes a covenant with Noah, his descendants, and every living creature: never again will a flood destroy all flesh or the earth.
promises.text: “As for me, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your offspring after you, and with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the earth with you, of all that go out of the ship, even every animal of the earth. I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
promises.context: God speaks to Noah and his sons after the flood.

promises.promise: The rainbow is God’s sign that he will remember his everlasting covenant and never again flood the world to destroy all flesh.
promises.text: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth. When I bring a cloud over the earth, that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud, I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and the waters will no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will look at it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.”
promises.context: God gives Noah a visible token of the flood covenant.

promises.promise: God will make Abram a great nation, bless him, make his name great, protect those who bless him, and bless all the earth’s families through him.
promises.text: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.
promises.context: Yahweh’s call to Abram to leave his country for a land God will show him.

promises.promise: God promises to give the land of Canaan to Abram’s offspring.
promises.text: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring.”
promises.context: At Shechem, after Abram entered Canaan.

promises.promise: God gives Abram all the land he can see, forever, and offspring as countless as the dust of the earth.
promises.text: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him, “Now, lift up your eyes, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward, for I will give all the land which you see to you and to your offspring forever. I will make your offspring as the dust of the earth, so that if a man can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring may also be counted. Arise, walk through the land in its length and in its width; for I will give it to you.”
promises.context: After Abram and Lot parted ways over grazing land.

promises.promise: God tells Abram not to fear: he himself is Abram’s shield and exceedingly great reward.
promises.text: After these things the LORD’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
promises.context: After Abram rescued Lot and refused the king of Sodom’s spoils.

promises.promise: Abram’s heir will be his own child, and his offspring will be as countless as the stars.
promises.text: Behold, the LORD’s word came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir, but he who will come out of your own body will be your heir.” The LORD brought him outside, and said, “Look now toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” He said to Abram, “So your offspring will be.”
promises.context: Abram had feared a household servant would be his heir.

promises.promise: God foretells oppression in a foreign land, then promises judgment on that nation and deliverance with great wealth.
promises.text: He said to Abram, “Know for sure that your offspring will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years. I will also judge that nation, whom they will serve. Afterward they will come out with great wealth.”
promises.context: During the covenant ceremony when Abram asked how he would know he would inherit the land.

promises.promise: God covenants to give Abram’s offspring the land from Egypt’s river to the Euphrates.
promises.text: In that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “I have given this land to your offspring, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates.”
promises.context: Sealed by God alone passing between the covenant pieces.

promises.promise: The angel of the LORD promises Hagar that her offspring will be greatly multiplied beyond counting.
promises.text: The angel of the LORD said to her, “I will greatly multiply your offspring, that they will not be counted for multitude.”
promises.context: Hagar fled from Sarai and met the angel of the LORD by a spring in the wilderness.

promises.promise: God renames Abram as Abraham, father of many nations, and pledges an everlasting covenant: to be their God and give Canaan as an everlasting possession.
promises.text: “As for me, behold, my covenant is with you. You will be the father of a multitude of nations. Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations. I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make nations of you. Kings will come out of you. I will establish my covenant between me and you and your offspring after you throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to you and to your offspring after you. I will give to you, and to your offspring after you, the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession. I will be their God.”
promises.context: When Abraham was ninety-nine years old, God appeared as God Almighty.

promises.promise: God renames Sarai as Sarah and promises her a son; she will be a mother of nations and kings.
promises.text: God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her name Sarai, but her name shall be Sarah. I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. Yes, I will bless her, and she will be a mother of nations. Kings of peoples will come from her.”
promises.context: Part of the same covenant appearance when Abraham was ninety-nine.

promises.promise: Sarah will bear Isaac, and God will establish an everlasting covenant with him and his offspring.
promises.text: God said, “No, but Sarah, your wife, will bear you a son. You shall call his name Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his offspring after him.”
promises.context: Abraham had asked that Ishmael might live before God.

promises.promise: God has heard Abraham concerning Ishmael: he will bless him, multiply him, and make him a great nation.
promises.text: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly. He will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
promises.context: God answers Abraham’s plea for Ishmael while confirming the covenant line through Isaac.

promises.promise: God promises that Sarah will have a son within a year.
promises.text: He said, “I will certainly return to you at about this time next year; and behold, Sarah your wife will have a son.”
promises.context: Three visitors appear to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre; Sarah listens from the tent.

promises.promise: Nothing is too hard for the LORD; he will return at the appointed time and Sarah will have a son.
promises.text: Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the set time I will return to you, when the season comes around, and Sarah will have a son.
promises.context: God responds after Sarah laughed at the promise of a child in old age.

promises.promise: God reassures Abraham that the covenant line will be named through Isaac, while also caring for Ishmael.
promises.text: God said to Abraham, “Don’t let it be grievous in your sight because of the boy, and because of your servant. In all that Sarah says to you, listen to her voice. For your offspring will be named through Isaac.”
promises.context: When Sarah asked Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away after Isaac’s weaning feast.

promises.promise: God hears Ishmael’s voice, tells Hagar not to fear, and promises to make a great nation of the boy.
promises.text: God heard the voice of the boy. The angel of God called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, “What troubles you, Hagar? Don’t be afraid. For God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him with your hand. For I will make him a great nation.”
promises.context: Hagar and Ishmael were cast out and wandering in the wilderness of Beersheba.

promises.promise: Because Abraham did not withhold Isaac, God swears to multiply his offspring like stars and sand, give them victory, and bless all nations through his offspring.
promises.text: ‘I have sworn by myself,’ says the LORD, ‘because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son, that I will bless you greatly, and I will multiply your offspring greatly like the stars of the heavens, and like the sand which is on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of his enemies. All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your offspring, because you have obeyed my voice.’
promises.context: After Abraham’s obedience on Mount Moriah when God provided a ram.

promises.promise: God will be with Isaac, bless him, give him the lands, multiply his offspring like the stars, and bless all nations through his offspring.
promises.text: Live in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you. For I will give to you, and to your offspring, all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father. I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the sky, and will give all these lands to your offspring. In your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
promises.context: During a famine, God tells Isaac not to go down to Egypt but to stay in the land.

promises.promise: God tells Isaac not to be afraid: he is with him, will bless him, and multiply his offspring for Abraham’s sake.
promises.text: The LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
promises.context: At Beersheba, after conflict over wells with the Philistines.

promises.promise: God gives Jacob the land and countless offspring, promises that all families will be blessed through him, and pledges his presence, protection, return, and faithfulness until every word is done.
promises.text: Behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you lie on to you and to your offspring. Your offspring will be as the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south. In you and in your offspring, all the families of the earth will be blessed. Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.”
promises.context: Jacob’s dream of the stairway at Bethel while fleeing from Esau.

promises.promise: God will keep Jacob wherever he goes, bring him home again, and never leave him until every promised word is fulfilled.
promises.text: Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.
promises.context: The heart of God’s word to Jacob in the Bethel dream—useful as a focused presence promise.

promises.promise: God tells Jacob to return to the land of his fathers and promises to be with him.
promises.text: The LORD said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”
promises.context: After years with Laban, when tension had grown over Jacob’s prosperity.

promises.promise: God renames Jacob as Israel, promises nations and kings from him, and confirms the land given to Abraham and Isaac.
promises.text: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel. God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body. The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”
promises.context: God appears again to Jacob at Bethel after he returned from Paddan Aram.

promises.promise: God tells Jacob not to fear going to Egypt: there he will make him a great nation, go down with him, and surely bring him up again.
promises.text: He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation. I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
promises.context: At Beersheba, as Jacob prepared to reunite with Joseph in Egypt during famine.

promises.promise: Jacob affirms God’s promise that God will be with Joseph and bring him again to the land of his fathers.
promises.text: Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.”
promises.context: Jacob blesses Joseph’s sons Ephraim and Manasseh near the end of his life.

promises.promise: Joseph trusts God’s sworn promise: God will surely visit his people and bring them up to the land promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
promises.text: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
promises.context: Joseph’s dying words in Egypt, looking forward to the exodus.

promises.promise: God has seen Israel’s affliction, heard their cry, and come down to deliver them into a good land flowing with milk and honey.
promises.text: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows. I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land to a good and large land, to a land flowing with milk and honey.”
promises.context: God reveals his compassion and rescue plan at Horeb.

promises.promise: God promises Moses his presence as the sign that he has sent him; Israel will worship on that mountain after deliverance.
promises.text: He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
promises.context: At the burning bush, when Moses felt inadequate for the call.

promises.promise: If Israel listens and keeps God’s ways, he will spare them the diseases of Egypt—for he is the LORD who heals them.
promises.text: He said, “If you will diligently listen to the LORD your God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you.”
promises.context: At Marah, after God made bitter water sweet for Israel in the wilderness.

promises.promise: God’s presence will go with his people and give them rest.
promises.text: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
promises.context: Moses pleaded that God not send Israel onward without his presence after the golden calf.

promises.promise: Be strong and courageous: the LORD goes with you; he will not fail you nor forsake you.
promises.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.
promises.context: Moses encourages Israel as they prepare to enter the land under Joshua.

promises.promise: God commands courage and promises his presence wherever Joshua goes.
promises.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
promises.context: God commissions Joshua after Moses’ death to lead Israel into Canaan.

promises.promise: The LORD shepherds his people so they lack nothing; even in the darkest valley his presence removes fear and brings comfort.
promises.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
promises.context: David’s psalm of trust in the LORD as shepherd.

promises.promise: God is a refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
promises.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
promises.context: A song of Zion celebrating God’s protection amid upheaval.

promises.promise: Those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength—soaring, running, and walking without collapse.
promises.text: but those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
promises.context: Comfort to weary exiles: the everlasting Creator does not faint.

promises.promise: Do not fear: God is with you, strengthens you, helps you, and upholds you with his righteous right hand.
promises.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
promises.context: God reassures Israel, his chosen servant, amid surrounding nations.

promises.promise: God who created and redeemed his people says not to fear; when they pass through waters and fire, he will be with them and they will not be consumed.
promises.text: But now the LORD who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine. When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.”
promises.context: A word of redemption and belonging to Israel in exile.

promises.promise: God’s thoughts toward his exiled people are of peace, not evil—to give them hope and a future.
promises.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says the LORD, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
promises.context: Part of a letter to Judean exiles in Babylon after seventy years were promised.

promises.promise: In the new covenant God will write his law on hearts, be their God, and forgive iniquity, remembering sin no more.
promises.text: “But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,” says the LORD: “I will put my law in their inward parts, and I will write it in their heart. I will be their God, and they shall be my people. They will no longer each teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD;’ for they will all know me, from their least to their greatest,” says the LORD, “for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.”
promises.context: The promise of a new covenant beyond the broken Sinai covenant.

promises.promise: Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to him for rest; his yoke is easy and his burden light.
promises.text: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.”
promises.context: Jesus’ invitation after thanking the Father for revealing truth to the humble.

promises.promise: As disciples make disciples of all nations, Jesus promises to be with them always, to the end of the age.
promises.text: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
promises.context: The Great Commission on the mountain in Galilee after the resurrection.

promises.promise: God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have eternal life.
promises.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
promises.context: Jesus’ conversation with Nicodemus about new birth and salvation.

promises.promise: Jesus tells troubled hearts to trust; he prepares a place and will come again to receive his own to himself.
promises.text: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me. In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you. If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.”
promises.context: Upper room discourse on the night before the cross.

promises.promise: Jesus gives his own peace—not as the world gives—and tells his followers not to let their hearts be troubled or fearful.
promises.text: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
promises.context: Jesus comforts the disciples as he prepares to leave them.

promises.promise: God works all things together for good for those who love him and are called according to his purpose.
promises.text: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
promises.context: Paul’s assurance amid suffering, as creation waits for redemption.

promises.promise: Nothing in all creation can separate believers from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus.
promises.text: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
promises.context: The climax of Romans 8 on security in God’s love.

promises.promise: God will supply every need of his people according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
promises.text: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
promises.context: Paul thanks the Philippians for their generous partnership in the gospel.

promises.promise: Anyone who lacks wisdom can ask God, who gives generously and without finding fault—and it will be given.
promises.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
promises.context: James encourages believers facing trials to seek God’s wisdom in faith.

promises.promise: God will dwell with his people forever; he will wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more.
promises.text: I heard a loud voice out of heaven saying, “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people; and he will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”
promises.context: Vision of the new heaven and new earth and the New Jerusalem.

promises.promise: The One on the throne declares that he is making all things new—and these words are faithful and true.
promises.text: He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” He said, “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
promises.context: God’s own declaration in the vision of the new creation.

promises.promise: The LORD himself goes before you; he will be with you and will never fail or forsake you—so do not be afraid or discouraged.
promises.text: Yahweh himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
promises.context: Moses encourages Joshua and Israel as leadership passes and they prepare to enter the land.

promises.promise: Even if father and mother abandon you, the LORD will take you up and care for you.
promises.text:
When my father and my mother forsake me,
then Yahweh will take me up.
promises.context: David’s trust that God’s care outlasts even the closest human relationships.

promises.promise: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted and saves those whose spirits are crushed.
promises.text:
Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart,
and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
promises.context: David’s praise after deliverance, assuring the hurting of God’s nearness and rescue.

promises.promise: Rest in the LORD and wait patiently; cease from anger and forsake wrath—fretting only leads to harm.
promises.text:
Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him.
Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way,
because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
Cease from anger, and forsake wrath.
Don’t fret, it leads only to evildoing.
promises.context: Wisdom for when the wicked seem to thrive and the heart burns with anger or envy.

promises.promise: Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you; he will not let the righteous be shaken.
promises.text:
Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you.
He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
promises.context: David under betrayal and distress, invited to throw the weight of trouble onto God.

promises.promise: The LORD is merciful and slow to anger; he does not treat us as our sins deserve, and removes our transgressions as far as east from west.
promises.text:
Yahweh is merciful and gracious,
slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.
He will not always accuse;
neither will he stay angry forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins,
nor repaid us for our iniquities.
For as the heavens are high above the earth,
so great is his loving kindness toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west,
so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
promises.context: David’s praise of God’s fatherly compassion and complete forgiveness.

promises.promise: God heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
promises.text:
He heals the broken in heart,
and binds up their wounds.
promises.context: A hymn celebrating God’s restoring care for his people and for the hurting.

promises.promise: Though sins are like scarlet, God invites reasoning together and promises they shall be white as snow.
promises.text:
“Come now, and let us reason together,” says Yahweh:
“Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow.
Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
promises.context: The LORD’s invitation to rebellious Judah: cleansing is available through his mercy.

promises.promise: Even if a mother could forget her nursing child, God will not forget you—he has engraved you on the palms of his hands.
promises.text:
“Can a woman forget her nursing child,
that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?
Yes, these may forget,
yet I will not forget you!
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands;
your walls are continually before me.
promises.context: God answers Zion’s fear of being forsaken with a deeper-than-maternal pledge of remembrance.

promises.promise: Mountains may move, but God’s loving kindness will not depart and his covenant of peace will not be removed.
promises.text:
For the mountains may depart,
and the hills be removed;
but my loving kindness will not depart from you,
and my covenant of peace will not be removed,”
says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
promises.context: Comfort to restored Zion: God’s mercy outlasts the most solid earthly landmarks.

promises.promise: God has loved his people with an everlasting love and draws them with loving kindness.
promises.text:
Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying,
“Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love.
Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.
promises.context: Assurance spoken into Israel’s exile: restoration rests on God’s unending love.

promises.promise: Because of the LORD’s loving kindnesses we are not consumed; his compassions never fail and are new every morning—great is his faithfulness.
promises.text:
It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed,
because his compassion doesn’t fail.
They are new every morning.
Great is your faithfulness.
promises.context: Hope rising from the ashes of Jerusalem’s fall: God’s mercy renews daily.

promises.promise: God pardons iniquity, does not stay angry forever, delights in mercy, and casts sins into the depths of the sea.
promises.text:
Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity,
and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage?
He doesn’t retain his anger forever,
because he delights in loving kindness.
He will again have compassion on us.
He will tread our iniquities under foot;
and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
promises.context: Micah’s closing praise of the pardoning God after judgment and promised restoration.

promises.promise: The LORD your God is among you as a mighty savior; he rejoices over you, calms you with his love, and sings over you.
promises.text: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
promises.context: Promise of joy over a restored remnant after judgment on Judah and the nations.

promises.promise: Those who mourn are blessed, for they will be comforted.
promises.text:
Blessed are those who mourn,
for they shall be comforted.
promises.context: Jesus’ Beatitudes speak comfort into grief as part of kingdom blessing.

promises.promise: Jesus will not leave his followers as orphans; he will come to them.
promises.text: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
promises.context: In the upper room, Jesus comforts disciples facing his departure.

promises.promise: There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
promises.text: There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.
promises.context: Paul’s gospel climax after wrestling with sin and the law: freedom from condemnation in Christ.

promises.promise: Do not take revenge; leave room for God’s justice—vengeance belongs to the Lord, and he will repay.
promises.text: Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God’s wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”
promises.context: Paul’s call to lived worship includes releasing personal vengeance into God’s hands.

promises.promise: The Father of mercies and God of all comfort comforts us in every affliction so we can comfort others.
promises.text:
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
promises.context: Paul opens with praise after severe trials in Asia, naming God as the source of real comfort.

promises.promise: God chose his people in Christ before the foundation of the world and predestined them for adoption as his children.
promises.text:
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love;
having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his desire,
promises.context: Paul’s doxology of every spiritual blessing in Christ begins with chosenness and adoption.

promises.promise: Instead of anxiety, bring everything to God in prayer with thanksgiving; his peace will guard your hearts and minds in Christ.
promises.text:
In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
promises.context: Paul’s pastoral close to the Philippians: prayer displaces anxiety with guarding peace.

promises.promise: God has said he will never leave you nor forsake you—so be content, free from the love of money.
promises.text: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
promises.context: Closing exhortations grounded in God’s unbreakable presence promise.

promises.promise: Cast all your worries on God, because he cares for you.
promises.text: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
promises.context: Peter urges humble trust under God’s mighty hand amid suffering.

promises.promise: If we confess our sins, God is faithful and righteous to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
promises.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
promises.context: John assures believers who walk in the light that confession meets faithful forgiveness.

promises.promise: Trust in the LORD with all your heart; acknowledge him in all your ways, and he will make your paths straight.
promises.text:
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart,
and don’t lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him,
and he will make your paths straight.
promises.context: Wisdom’s call to wholehearted trust when human insight is not enough.
